_comment: Copy to rag-eval.json and replace these with questions about YOUR corpus.
A dozen questions you already know the answers to is enough to start, and
far more useful than none: it turns 'this change feels better' into a
number. Add one every time a search disappoints you - a golden set built
from real failures is worth more than one invented up front.
question  what someone would actually type, in their words rather than
the document's. Questions phrased in the document's own
wording pass trivially and measure nothing.
expect    substrings matched against the result path. Any one counts as
a hit. Substrings rather than exact citations on purpose:
line ranges shift whenever chunking changes, and a golden set
needing a rewrite after every change will not be maintained.
note      why this question is here. Future you will not remember.
...make a change, reindex if it touches embedding...

questions.question: how do I rotate the signing certificate?
questions.note: the phrase people actually use; the runbook says 'renew', not 'rotate'

questions.question: what is the retention period for audit logs?
questions.note: a specific fact with exactly one right source

questions.question: INC-4471
questions.note: an exact identifier - this is what the keyword arm exists for, and it should never miss

questions.question: who approves an exception to the change freeze?
questions.note: more than one document may legitimately answer; any is a hit

questions.question: why did we move off the shared database?
questions.note: reasoning rather than a fact - the kind of question embeddings are for
